content: All individuals diagnosed with diabetes should undergo an evaluation for diabetic peripheral neuropathy. For those with type 2 diabetes, this assessment should occur at the time of diagnosis. For individuals with type 1 diabetes, the evaluation should take place five years after the initial diagnosis. Following these initial assessments, annual screenings for diabetic peripheral neuropathy are recommended. The evaluation for neuropathy should include specific tests to assess temperature sensation or pinprick sensation, as well as vibration perception. Vibration perception should be tested using a 128-Hz tuning fork to ensure accurate assessment of sensory function. Diabetic neuropathies encompass a wide range of disorders that affect both the peripheral nervous system and the autonomic nervous system. It is important to note that up to 50% of cases of diabetic peripheral neuropathy may be asymptomatic. However, even in the absence of symptoms, these conditions can lead to serious complications, such as foot ulcers, if not properly managed. Maintaining optimal glycemic control has been shown to slow the progression of diabetic peripheral neuropathy. However, it is important to understand that glycemic control does not reverse the nerve damage that has already occurred.
